key_insight: For D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr on DSS 2205, increasing spray distance to 190 mm produced the densest coating and the best corrosion resistance in acidic media.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance is a practical process lever for improving coating integrity and extending the service life of stainless-steel components exposed to strong acids.
method: D-gun spray Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm stand-off distances.
Expose coated samples to 1 M H2SO4 at room temperature.
Evaluate OCP, EIS, potentiodynamic polarization, and SEM/porosity.
Compare coating microstructure and corrosion rate against the uncoated substrate.
evidence_signal: SEM showed porosity dropped from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, and the 190 mm coating achieved the lowest corrosion rate (0.113 mmpy) versus 2.60 mmpy for the bare substrate.
watch_item: The reported optimum is specific to this coating system, acid concentration, and test conditions, so performance may shift under different service environments or spray parameters.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
